title: Event corrections nearly close the 2001-2022 AMIP SST warming gap but preserve a feedback gap in five linear models
abstract: We tested the released PCMDI-AMIP-OI2p1 1.0 prototype against AMIP 1.1.9 on a fixed ice-free 60S-60N ocean mask. We applied five published linear Green's functions and paired the published input-event correction maps for both SST histories. The new forcing retains a July 2020 warm step of 0.090 C against ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2, while its old July 2018 Southern Ocean step estimate is small and uncertain. In 2001-2022, the central event correction removes 93% of the SST-trend gap and 64% of the SST-induced radiative-trend gap. The corrected SST trends are 0.134 and 0.129 K per decade. Yet the five-model mean feedback gap becomes more negative, from -0.267 to -0.368 W m-2 K-1 of ocean SST. Across 20 map choices, corrections remove 83-111% of the warming gap and 57-70% of the radiative gap. We derive exact feedback bounds by evaluating vertices of event-amplitude boxes. With every event varied independently from half to twice its published amplitude, the five-model mean feedback gap remains negative for all 20 map choices, with a total bound of -1.035 to -0.061 W m-2 K-1. The corresponding 1982-2022 bound includes zero. The recent remaining flux gap is mainly tropical. This conditional result shows that agreement in ocean-mean warming does not ensure agreement in model feedback. The maps are uncertain and are transferred to a new processed product. Bounds keep map shapes and dates fixed. The calculation excludes sea ice, polar SST, smooth error drift, nonlinear response and global air-temperature normalization. It does not determine the true SST history or observed feedback. Code, analytical series, numerical checks and exact source hashes are included.

display.caption: Published event corrections nearly close the recent SST-trend gap but leave a feedback gap. All values use a fixed ice-free 60S-60N mask and five linear models. Error bars are conditional on fixed maps.

The released prototype retains the 2020 warm step. The remaining modeled radiative pattern difference has contributions from the tropical Indian Ocean, east Pacific and Southern Ocean. Product differences do not identify the true SST error.
Shared-amplitude stress tests can erase the remaining radiation-trend gap. The feedback gap stays negative. The text also gives exact bounds with independent amplitudes for each event.
